text: This service reads party flags, deceased and bankrupt markers, case facts and batch freshness only through the rwb-source-data contract, and keeps the FSD's field names as the source field names that contract returns.
why: Architecture v5 is higher in precedence than the FSD and makes the 30 recovery.v_ace_* views readable by rwb-source-data alone; the slide 13 matrix gives the S8 row one R and one E to P1 and no other data cell.
read: The FSD's integration points and its nine stale-data validation rows as a statement of which facts each step needs, not of how they are read.
applied_in: Section 2.4 constraint 1; Section 5.1; Section 6 FR-S8-045 and FR-S8-046; Section 8.2; Section 8.4 rule 2; Section 9
confirm: Solution architect with P1, before the wave 2 system test
impact: If a view stays readable by this service, the boundary test and the freshness guarantee need a second owner.

text: The stage-clock pause, the prescription clock and the resume are durable timers inside DeviationWorkflow through the Temporal workflow kit, and no Quartz table, connection or job is a dependency of this service.
why: Architecture v5 and the Temporal design replace Quartz with event-started workflows and durable timers, and Template and Rules R6 retires the Quartz story.
read: The three 'Workbench, Quartz scheduler' integration rows as a statement that these steps are timed, not as a statement of the timer technology.
applied_in: Section 2.3; Section 2.4 constraint 6; Section 6 FR-S8-006; Section 9; Section 10.1
confirm: Solution architect, before the S8 contract story closes
impact: A Quartz dependency would put a shared scheduler inside a per-case wait and lose the paused state on a restart.

text: The raise and the clear are the two commands the Ownership Map records, the deviation read is one synchronous GET served by this service and reached through gateway-bff, and no path beyond those is fixed by this document.
why: The Architecture slide, the Ownership Map and the FSD name the operations three different ways, and the FSD times a read that no source records.
read: The slide 15 contract, the map's two endpoints and the FSD's two second timeout as one intent: a command to raise, a command to clear and a read for the case record.
applied_in: Section 2.4 constraint 4; Section 6 FR-S8-001 and FR-S8-019; Section 9; Section 9.1; Section 12 OQ-S8-01
confirm: Solution architect, before the S8 contract story closes
impact: The screen and the case record composite route cannot be built until one path wins.

text: This service owns five entity groups in schema rwb_deviation: deviation, which the Ownership Map names, and screening run, screening score, contact stop and breach record, which are named as product entities and have no physical table name in this document.
why: The map has one S8 table and Architecture v5 describes the schema as screening, pause, handling and return; the FSD's criteria require a run, a score, a stop and a breach record.
read: Architecture v5's description of the schema contents and the FSD's criteria as the entity set, with the physical names left to the DB story.
applied_in: Section 8.1; Section 10.5; Section 12 OQ-S8-02
confirm: Data architect, before the S8 DB story
impact: The migration and the boundary test cannot be written until the table set exists; no story is blocked by it in wave 2.

text: The approval a deviation carries is taken inside DeviationWorkflow by the role that the deviation code assigns, and it is recorded through the decision-record library and the shared decision record topic, without a P7 ApprovalWorkflow edge.
why: The FSD records an approver and a decision log entry, while the S8 row has no P7 cell and Architecture v5 places ApprovalWorkflow on rwb-valuation and rwb-decision only.
read: The FSD's approval record as an attribute of the deviation decision, and the matrix's empty P7 cell as the absence of a separate approval workflow, not of an approval.
applied_in: Section 2.4 constraint 11; Section 6 FR-S8-009, FR-S8-015 and FR-S8-048; Section 9; Section 12 OQ-S8-03
confirm: Solution architect with the S8 business analyst, before the wave 2 system test
impact: A wrong carrier turns a two-role step into a single-role one, which is the control the FSD is protecting.

text: Every external effect of this service (the fraud referral, the bureau and agency skip trace, the claim filing with the receiver or the Legal Execution Department, the insurance claim and the re-appraisal) is a contract dependency on rwb-integration or on the owning service's contract, built against its published fake.
why: The FSD names five outside systems and the partner portal while the S8 row has neither an rwb-integration cell nor an outside cell, and DP-16 makes the integration contract the only carrier of an outside call.
read: The FSD's integration points as the set of outside capabilities each flow needs, with the carrier left to the contract of the owning service.
applied_in: Section 2.3; Section 5.1; Section 6 FR-S8-037, FR-S8-039 and FR-S8-054; Section 9; Section 9.1; Section 12 OQ-S8-04
confirm: Solution architect with the integration lead, before the wave 4 test
impact: A direct call from this service breaks the one-hop rule and puts an outside timeout inside a per-case wait.

text: The screening agent reads documents through the rwb-document contract and call notes through the rwb-source-data contract, and schema rwb_deviation holds no copy of a document and no free text from a call note.
why: Every screening criterion is given documents and call notes while the S8 row has no P5 cell and no source names the call notes as a data product.
read: The criteria's population description as the input set of the screening step, with the carrier left to the two owners that already hold the data.
applied_in: Section 5.1; Section 6 FR-S8-021 and FR-S8-024; Section 8.2; Section 8.4 rule 3; Section 9
confirm: Solution architect with the P5 and P1 owners, before the shadow screening test
impact: An unowned read either duplicates a document store or puts personal data in the deviation schema.

text: Each FSD criterion row is carried as one criterion with its ID unchanged, and where a row asserts the case record view rather than the behaviour it sits under, this PRD adds its own step criterion and keeps the source row as the evidence.
why: Seven of the nine E2 features repeat the same 'Timers shown' scenario on the case record story, so the source row cannot prove the behaviour by itself.
read: The repeated rows as one criterion on the case record view of story RWB-E2-015, not as nine separate proofs.
applied_in: Section 6; Section 11.1; Section 11.3
confirm: Business analyst, S8 with the QA lead, before the wave 2 test
impact: Without an added step criterion the pause, the stop and the resume pass review with no test behind them.

text: The ten E7 features keep their placeholder criterion 'Written one epic ahead' in the evidence column, and their acceptance tests are written when the E7 stories are groomed rather than invented here.
why: The FSD states the placeholder for every E7 feature and no alternate flow, while the BRD specifies the capability and its story key.
read: The placeholder as a deliberate deferral of the acceptance test, not as an absence of the requirement.
applied_in: Section 10.4; Section 11.1; Section 11.3
confirm: Business analyst, S8 with the QA lead, before the wave 4 test
impact: The wave 4 slices cannot be signed off until those tests exist; the requirement itself is not blocked.

text: The deceased customer slice lands twice on purpose: the contact stop, the heir and estate notification and the insurance claim path as the E3 slice in wave 2, and the full X3 flow with its approver and return point in wave 4.
why: The program and the FSD tag the requirement E3, the BRD tags the feature E7, and the BRD's Q-015 leaves the choice open.
read: Both tags as one requirement served twice, which is what the BRD's own assumption ASM-022 already says.
applied_in: Section 5; Section 10.2; Section 10.3; Section 10.4; Section 12 OQ-S8-05
confirm: Product Owner, answering Q-015
impact: A single home for X3 would either delay the E3 conduct control or drop the E7 approver.

text: The twelve R-DEV rules the FSD names, plus R-DEV-19 to R-DEV-21 from the Temporal design, are the requirement set of this service; the remaining rules of the twenty-two are package authoring in rwb-decision.
why: The FSD names twelve rules and the design names three more and states the route set is twenty-two rules whose package is Phase 2 with no owner.
read: The design's rule IDs as requirements because the design outranks the FSD, and the package itself as governance work outside this document.
applied_in: Section 2.4 constraint 7; Section 6 FR-S8-005, FR-S8-013 and FR-S8-044; Section 9; Section 10.5
confirm: Center of excellence analyst with P7, before the wave 2 test
impact: A missing rule leaves a code with no owner or a deviation with no escalation, which are the two controls the module exists for.

text: The deviation service level, the ten working day escalation and the thirty day skip trace window are versioned reference data read at run time; no number is asserted in this document.
why: The FSD sets the target cell to 'Set with DL22' in every feature and states no period, and the design is the only source for the ten and thirty day figures.
read: The metric row as a requirement to hold a service level, not as the value of one.
applied_in: Section 6 FR-S8-044 and FR-S8-049; Section 7 NFR-S8-009; Section 12 OQ-S8-06
confirm: Business lead, setting DL22
impact: A hard-coded service level would make a policy change a release, which BR-S8-00n forbids.

text: The confidence threshold that sends a flag to a person and the autonomy policy that permits L1 on a segment are held as versioned reference data by rwb-agent and rwb-decision; this service reads them and asserts no value.
why: The FSD names the policy, its version and the evaluation sample but states no threshold, and the BRD leaves the autonomy evidence to Q-014 and BR-084.
read: The policy reference in the criterion (policy SCREENING version P2, status LOADED) as the mechanism, with the numbers held by their owners.
applied_in: Section 6 FR-S8-028 and FR-S8-049; Section 7 NFR-S8-013; Section 12 OQ-S8-07
confirm: Risk and model risk officer with the P10 owner, before the L1 run
impact: A mis-set threshold either floods the review queue or lets an agent change a case unread.

text: The deviation record, the screening run and the breach record are confidential records attached to a case; the staff identifier of the handler is confidential rather than personal customer data, and no retention period is stated.
why: The FSD marks all eight fields as not personal data and gives no classification or retention, and DL26 and Q-012 are open.
read: The personal data column of the field catalog as a statement that no customer personal data is held in the record, not as a statement that the record needs no classification.
applied_in: Section 8.1; Section 8.3; Section 8.4 rule 6; Section 12 OQ-S8-08
confirm: Compliance and PDPA officer, closing DL26 and Q-012
impact: An unclassified record cannot be scheduled for disposal and cannot be defended in an audit.

text: The raise screen and the deviation queue are gateway-bff composite routes over this service's read and command contract, and this service owns neither screen.
why: The Ownership Map records no screen and no composite route for S8, and DP-19 makes every screen an edge composite route.
read: The two screens as product views of this service's contract, with the composition owned at the edge.
applied_in: Section 4; Section 6 FR-S8-018 and FR-S8-020; Section 9; Section 12 OQ-S8-09
confirm: Solution architect with the platform edge owner, before the wave 2 screen test
impact: A screen built inside the service would duplicate the edge pattern and break the single sign-on path.

text: Every message ID is preserved and served from the message catalogue in Thai and in English, the English wording that the FSD gives is kept character for character, and the Thai wording and the approver are left to DL10.
why: The FSD names eight messages, gives the English wording of three, and names no approver; NFR-059 requires both languages.
read: The message ID as the stable reference and the wording as content that the catalogue owns.
applied_in: Section 6 FR-S8-019; Section 7 NFR-S8-022; Section 11.1; Section 12 OQ-S8-10
confirm: Business analyst, S8, closing DL10
impact: A message rendered from code fails the bilingual requirement and the wording control.

text: DeviationRaised and DeviationCleared are carried by name and topic, keyed by the case, as CloudEvents 1.0 through the outbox, with the code, the state, the contact stop flag, the return point and the decision record reference in the payload and no personal and no financial value.
why: The catalogue gives the two events a row, an owner and a topic but no field list, while the criteria expect an agent verdict and a decision record entry to be readable against the deviation.
read: The catalogue rows as the event identity and the criteria as the payload content a consumer needs.
applied_in: Section 6 FR-S8-013 and FR-S8-014; Section 7 NFR-S8-017; Section 9; Section 12 OQ-S8-11
confirm: Solution architect, writing the AsyncAPI contract with the contract story
impact: A consumer that must read the deviation back needs the read operation to exist, which gap 3 leaves open.

text: No deviation, screening or queue volume is asserted; the population figures of the non-functional specification and the two evaluation samples of 200 and 500 cases are the only quantities used.
why: The module states no volume and the only numbers in it are the two sample sizes, while NFR-001 and NFR-002 give the case and user populations of the platform.
read: The sample sizes as evaluation populations, not as production volumes.
applied_in: Section 7 NFR-S8-008; Section 11.3
confirm: Solution architect, after the shadow run measures the real deviation rate
impact: A volume test sized on an invented figure either over-builds or fails in production.

text: This document is Draft and no approval is recorded in this run. The BRD is read as approved for the purpose of writing the PRD, and the missing Product Owner and FDA decisions are carried as this assumption.
why: The D-RCV-60 overlay forbids a stop for approval and requires a missing approval or status to be recorded as an assumption and the document to continue in Draft.
read: The BRD's governance table as not read in this run; no approval row is asserted that a source does not contain.
applied_in: Section 1.1 status; Section 13
confirm: Product Owner and FDA, by approving this PRD
impact: A reader must not treat the contents as approved requirements until the approval table is signed.

text: The service is wave 2. EP02 and EP03 are wave 2 and EP07 is wave 4, so the E2 and E3 slices land with the service in wave 2 and the E7 flows land after it in wave 4; no wave conflict is raised.
why: The service table, the wave map and the program's requirement-to-service table all place this service at wave 2 with EP02, EP03 and EP07, and R5.6 raises a conflict only where a story's wave is earlier than its service's wave.
read: The three business epics as three release slices of one service rather than three waves of one service.
applied_in: Section 1.1; Section 10; Section 11.2
confirm: Programme manager, at release planning
impact: None on the requirements; the wave 4 slice must not be promised in the December release.

text: The identifier families of this document (CAP, FR, NFR, AC, JRN, ROL and OQ with the S8 prefix) are new and exist only here; every FSD identifier (REQ, FEAT, AC, VR, BR-S8, R-DEV, MSG, LOV, SCR) and every BRD identifier (REQ, BR, RULE, Q, DL) is preserved character for character.
why: The PRD is the first document of its family for this service, and the source IDs are the trace the stories and the tests are written from.
read: The FSD and BRD identifiers as immutable keys, and the PRD's own identifiers as new keys that point at them.
applied_in: Section 1.3; Section 5; Section 6; Section 11
confirm: Traceability manager, at the D1 numbering step
impact: A changed source ID would break the trace to the stories and to the FSD.

text: The change notes and dates of FSD S8 versions 1 and 2 are not in the sources read and are carried as 'Not specified in the source documents' rather than reconstructed.
why: Only FSD S8 v3 is present in the extract folder and its change note refers back to v2 without restating it.
read: The v3 change note as the boundary of what this document can assert about the earlier versions.
applied_in: Section 1.3
confirm: Business analyst, S8, when the folder is completed
impact: None on the requirements; the history table is incomplete until then.
